concept_options.title: The Bulge Nobody Can Explain
concept_options.hook: Everyone knows the Moon lifts the sea. Nobody can tell you why it also rises on the opposite side.
concept_options.visual_approach: A page from a physics book, corrected in front of you. Warm paper, ink line work, one blue for water and one vermilion for force. The familiar two-bulge diagram is drawn, then struck through, then replaced by three arrows of unequal length across the planet - which is the whole explanation and needs no words.
concept_options.target_audience: Anyone who has stood on a beach and half-remembers a diagram from school.
key_points: Two high tides a day, and the far-side one is the puzzle
The answer you were taught - centrifugal force - is a fictitious force in a rotating frame, and the literature calls it a misconception
Nothing pushes: the Moon pulls the near ocean hardest, the Earth less, the far ocean least
So the planet is pulled out from under its own far-side water
The tide is not gravity being strong. It is gravity being uneven.
concept_options.core_message: A tide is not the Moon pulling hard. It is the Moon pulling unevenly - and the far side rises because the Earth is dragged away from it.
concept_options.tone: corrective, unhurried, quietly delighted by the fix
grounded_in: arXiv: textbooks breed the centrifugal misconception
underserved_gaps: the far side is always a footnote
concept_options.why_this_works: The far-side bulge is a question the audience already half-holds and has never had answered. The correction is short, drawable in three arrows, and backed by both NOAA and a peer-reviewed audit of how textbooks get it wrong.

concept_options.title: The Moon Is Leaving, And You Are Paying For It
concept_options.hook: Every tide takes a little spin out of the planet. The Moon is 3.83 centimetres further away than last year.
concept_options.visual_approach: A ledger, literally: an accounting page where energy moves from one column to another. The Earth's rotation is debited, the Moon's orbit credited, and a laser line runs off the top of the frame to the mirrors Apollo left behind.
concept_options.target_audience: People who like a number with a consequence attached.
key_points: The bulges are dragged slightly ahead of the Moon by the planet's rotation
Their gravity tows the Moon forward, and friction bleeds spin out of the Earth
The day lengthens by about 1.6 milliseconds a century
The Moon recedes 3.83 cm a year, measured by laser off Apollo retroreflectors
concept_options.core_message: The tide is a transaction, and the receipt is measurable to a hundredth of a centimetre.
grounded_in: PMC: 1.6-1.7 ms/century, 3.83 +/- 0.008 cm/yr, lunar laser ranging
concept_options.why_this_works: One extraordinary number that is precisely measured, with an Apollo hook. But it assumes the viewer already accepts the bulges, which is exactly what they do not understand.

concept_options.title: Why Your Bathtub Has No Tide
concept_options.hook: The Moon pulls your bathwater exactly as hard as it pulls the Pacific. Only one of them moves.
concept_options.visual_approach: Two vessels side by side for the whole video - a bath and an ocean - with the same arrows drawn on both. The arrows on the bath are identical to each other; the arrows on the ocean are not. That single difference is the entire film.
concept_options.target_audience: People who want the mechanism isolated rather than the phenomenon described.
key_points: Gravity's strength is not what makes a tide
What matters is how much it changes across the thing being pulled
A bath is too small for the difference to exist
An ocean is 12,000 km wide, and that is the whole story
concept_options.core_message: Tides are made of difference, not force.
grounded_in: NASA: small bodies of water have no tides
common_questions: why doesn't my bathtub have tides
concept_options.why_this_works: The cleanest isolation of the mechanism, and it answers a real forum question. Risk: without the far-side puzzle it is a definition rather than a revelation.

concept_options.title: There Is No Bulge
concept_options.hook: The diagram in your textbook shows a wave of water circling the planet. It cannot exist.
concept_options.visual_approach: Start by animating the familiar diagram faithfully, then run the numbers on it live on screen until it breaks: a free wave tops out around 330 m/s, the equator turns at 465, and the drawing tears.
concept_options.target_audience: Viewers who already know the standard model and enjoy having it dismantled.
key_points: A tidal bulge would be a shallow-water wave half the planet's circumference long
Such a wave cannot exceed about 330 m/s even over the deepest trench
The equator moves at 465 m/s, so nothing can keep up
Real tides are basin resonances, not a bulge sliding around the world
concept_options.core_message: The picture everyone uses is a teaching fiction, and the real answer is stranger.
grounded_in: PhysicsForums: free wave speed versus rotational speed
concept_options.why_this_works: The most genuinely surprising claim available, and the riskiest: it demolishes a model the audience does not yet hold correctly. Better as a follow-up than as an introduction.

selected_concept.rationale: T1 answers the question the audience is actually carrying, and the answer fits in one drawing - three arrows of unequal length. T3's mechanism ('difference, not force') is the same insight stated abstractly, so it folds in as the closing line rather than running as its own video. T2 and T4 both assume the viewer already accepts the bulges, which is the thing this video has to establish first; they stay on the shelf as sequels, in that order.
modifications: Fold T3's payoff into the last beat: a tide is made of difference, not force.
Borrow one shot from T2 as the closing image - the Moon drifting out of frame - so the video ends on a consequence rather than a summary.
The familiar diagram is drawn correctly first and then interrogated. Never mock it; the viewer learned it in good faith.

production_plan.art_direction: An engraved plate from a physics book, redrawn and corrected in front of you. Warm paper ground (#EDE6D6) with a faint deckle grain, everything set in ink (#141210) line work with visible construction lines - the drawing shows its own working. Water is a single deep sea blue (#1F4E6B); force is vermilion (#C1452F) and appears nowhere else, so every red mark on screen is a force. Language is set in a serif, including the numbers, because this is a page rather than an instrument. Ink draws on with a small overshoot and settles, the way a hand draws; nothing moves at constant velocity. The video does not end still - the Moon keeps drifting out of frame after the last word.

taste_profile.design_read: A page being corrected. Warm, patient, made of paper and ink rather than glass and light - the register of someone showing you the working, not of an instrument reporting a measurement.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Paper ground, ink line, one blue for water, one vermilion reserved exclusively for force. No fourth colour, no fills except water.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Full-bleed plate with a centred body · a struck-through wrong diagram · body with three unequal arrows · the same arrows with the middle one subtracted · a lunar-day clock face · a wide field with the Moon small and leaving.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Historical celestial-mechanics engravings as the register; no AI imagery and no stock footage - every mark is drawn by the composition.
anti_patterns: Anything from the previous video: dark ground, cyan/amber signal pair, a running counter, waveforms on a grid, a still final frame
Monospace type - this is a page, not a readout
Photographic space imagery or a realistic Earth
quality_gates: A viewer with the sound off must be able to reach the answer from the arrows alone
Vermilion may only ever mean force
The last shot must still be moving
No layout may be recognisable from the previous production

voice_selection.rationale: Still the only TTS configured on this machine, and still free and offline. Unchanged from the previous production, which is a real limitation rather than a choice: the environment has no cloud TTS key.
voice_selection.delivery_style: warmer and slower than the previous video - this one is a correction offered, not a measurement reported
voice_selection.pacing_policy: Longer sentences than last time, and one deliberate pause before the correction lands.

music_source.mood_direction: Deliberately no bed under most of the video. The previous production used a pulse; this one uses the absence of one, so the two do not share a sound. A single low swell arrives only at the closing beat.

stages.approach: Narration synthesised locally with Piper. No music bed except one self-produced swell at the end. Every visual hand-authored as TSX in the project's own Remotion composition.

tools.why_this_provider: The only TTS on this machine; local and free.

tools.role: would supply real footage of a tide
tools.why_this_provider: Unavailable twice over: no API key, and every Pexels host is denied by this environment's network policy (verified). Recorded rather than hidden. It would not have been used here anyway - a shot of a beach cannot show a force gradient - but a later video about the Bay of Fundy would genuinely want it.

stages.fallback_if_unavailable: If Piper cannot synthesise, the run stops and the blocker is reported.

stages.approach: Render the hand-authored composition through video_compose in atelier mode, then mux narration. 1080x1920, 30 fps.

tools.why_this_provider: Atelier mode renders a project-local composition and bypasses the stock scene registry, with a stock-reuse scan enforcing it.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Narration: Piper again (free, local, flat) vs a cloud voice
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Same ceiling as last time. This is now the clearest single upgrade available to the channel and it costs one environment variable.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Music: a bed under the whole video vs almost none
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: Quieter and less conventionally 'produced'. Chosen partly so this video does not share a sound signature with the previous one - sameness is not only visual.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Visuals: real footage of tides vs drawing every mark
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: No photographic texture. But the subject is a force gradient, which no camera can photograph; footage would decorate rather than explain.

alternative_paths.description: Free path (selected): Piper narration, one self-produced swell, hand-authored Remotion atelier composition.
alternative_paths.what_changes: Nothing is paid for. Voice is the weak point.

alternative_paths.description: Budget path: same visuals, cloud TTS.
alternative_paths.what_changes: The narration stops sounding synthetic. Needs one key that is not in this environment.

alternative_paths.description: Standard path: cloud TTS plus real Bay of Fundy footage for the scale beat.
alternative_paths.what_changes: One photographic beat against the drawn plate. Needs a Pexels key AND the network policy opened - both currently absent.

approval.user_notes: Standing pre-authorisation, reaffirmed in this session: the user asked for the next video to be produced here, with full decision authority and nothing asked. Every gated stage is recorded as approved under that authorisation, with the reasoning written into the decision log so it stays reviewable afterwards. As with the previous production, AGENT_GUIDE.md asks for an 'approval_policy' decision_log category that the schema enum does not contain, so it is recorded here.

metadata.divergence_from_previous: All five ledger fields differ from how-headphones-erase-sound: paper ground instead of near-black, ink/blue/vermilion instead of cyan/amber, three unequal arrows instead of a running counter, plate layouts instead of axes and traces, hand-drawn settle instead of constant velocity. Narrative structure and type family differ too, and the video ends moving rather than still.
